library(nlmixr2lib)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Du_2026_cendakimab"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Du_2026_cendakimab"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1002/psp4.70199>

Du 2026 models dysphagia days (DD), the number of days with dysphagia
symptoms in a two-week diary window, in patients with eosinophilic
esophagitis (EoE) treated with placebo or the anti-IL-13 antibody cendakimab
in the phase 3 study CC-93538-EE-001. A count `k` out of `n` evaluable diary
days follows a combined uniform-binomial (CUB) distribution:

`P(k | n) = pi * Binomial(k | n, xi) + (1 - pi) / (n + 1)`

The daily dysphagia probability `xi` is driven by a latent disease variable on
the logit scale,

`logit(xi) = BASE_i - Pmax * (1 - PBO(t)) - Emax * (1 - DE(t))`,

where `PBO(t) = exp(-kPBOKON * t)` is the placebo onset and `DE(t)` is a
turnover variable (`DE(0) = 1`, onset and offset rate `kDEKON`) whose
production is inhibited by the serum cendakimab concentration,
`Cp / (EC50 + Cp)`. Baseline counts are conditioned on the enrolment
criterion `DD >= 4`.

The analysis was sequential. Individual cendakimab concentrations were
generated from the empirical Bayes PK parameters of a population PK model
that the paper does not show, and the Supporting Information NONMEM code
reads those parameters (`CLi`, `VCi`, `Qi`, `VPi`, `KAi`, `ALAG1i`, `F1i`)
from the dataset. The packaged model does the same: the PK states are in
`model()` and the per-subject PK parameters are covariate columns
(`CL_INDIV`, `VC_INDIV`, `Q_INDIV`, `VP_INDIV`, `KA_INDIV`, `TLAG_INDIV`,
`FDEPOT_INDIV`). No cendakimab population PK model has been published, so
this vignette drives the model with an illustrative typical PK built by the
maintainers to reproduce the simulated concentration profiles of Du 2026
Figure 2 (see "Illustrative PK" below). It is not the authors' PK model.

The likelihood is encoded exactly with `ll(dysphagia_days)`. Supply the
observed count as `DV` and the number of evaluable diary days as `NDAYS`;
the time origin is the first dose (the NONMEM `TIME` is "time after first
dose"), and records at `time <= 0` are baseline records.

# Population

Du 2026 Table 1 summarises the 427 subjects of study CC-93538-EE-001 who
received at least one dose and had at least one post-baseline DD assessment:
143 on placebo, 143 on cendakimab 360 mg SC once weekly (QW) for 48 weeks and
141 on 360 mg QW for 24 weeks followed by 360 mg every two weeks (QW/Q2W).
Median age was 35 years (range 13 to 72; 34 adolescents), median body weight
81.0 kg (41.8 to 176.9), 30.4% were female and 91.3% were White. 66.3% were
steroid inadequate responders or intolerant (Steroid IR/I), the randomisation
stratification factor that the final model carries on Emax, and 33.7% had a
history of esophageal dilation. Enrolment required at least 4 dysphagia days
in the baseline two-week window. The same information is stored in the model
metadata:

```{r population}
str(rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Du_2026_cendakimab"))$population)
```

# Source trace

| Model element | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| CUB probability mass function | `pi * Binomial(k | n, xi) + (1 - pi) / (n + 1)` | Equation 1; Data S1 `$ERROR` `PDF` |
| Logit link and latent variable | `logit(xi) = BASE_i - fp(t) - fd(t)` | Equation 2; Data S1 `IPREF = BASE + PBOEFF + DEEFF` with negative effects |
| Placebo effect | `dPBO/dt = -kPBOKON * PBO`, `PBO(0) = 1`, `fp = Pmax * (1 - PBO)` | Equations 3-4; Data S1 `DADT(4)` |
| Drug effect | `dDE/dt = kDEKON * (1 - Cp / (EC50 + Cp)) - kDEKON * DE`, `DE(0) = 1`, `fd = Emax * (1 - DE)` | Equations 5-6; Data S1 `DADT(5)` |
| Baseline truncation | `P(k >= 4) = pi * (1 - BinomialCDF(3)) + (1 - pi) * (n - 3) / (n + 1)` | Equations 7-8; Data S1 `CDFLB` |
| Logit-transformed IIV on BASE | `BASE_i = BASE + (expit(LGT1 + eta) - expit(LGT1)) * LGT2` | Equations 9-10; Data S1 `ETABASET` (see Errata) |
| Covariate on Pmax | `Pmax_i = Pmax + (BASE_i - BASE) * BASEPmax` | Methods 'Interindividual Variability and Covariate Model Development'; Data S1 `COVBASEPMAX` |
| Covariate on Emax | `Emax_i = exp(log(Emax) + SIRINEmax * SIRIN)` | Data S1 `EMAX = EXP(LOG(POPEMAX)+COVSIRINEMAX)` |
| Half-life to rate constant | `k = log(2) / (168 * t_half[weeks])` per hour | Data S1 `POPPBOKON`, `POPDEKON` |
| PK structure | depot (lag, F1) -> central <-> peripheral, linear elimination | Data S1 `$MODEL`, `$PK`, `$DES` |
| `logitrbase` (BASE) | 4.521 | Table 2 |
| `lkpbo` | log(log(2) / (168 * 27.66)) | Table 2: half-life of PBO onset 27.66 weeks |
| `lpmax` | log(8.092) | Table 2 |
| `lkout` | log(log(2) / (168 * 1.408)) | Table 2: half-life of drug onset 1.408 weeks |
| `lemax` | log(1.865) | Table 2 |
| `lec50` | 4.337 (EC50 = 76.5 ug/mL) | Table 2 |
| `logitskew_logitrbase` (LGT1) | -2.419 | Table 2 |
| `logitwidth_logitrbase` (LGT2) | 61.24 | Table 2 |
| `logitpinform` (pi, logit scale) | 2.568 | Table 2; Data S1 `PIP = EXP(PIPT)/(1+EXP(PIPT))` |
| `e_logitrbase_pmax` (BASEPmax) | 0.9115 | Table 2 |
| `e_steroid_ir_emax` (SIRINEmax) | 0.2377 | Table 2 |
| `etalogitrbase`, `etalkpbo` | variances 4.309 and 4.041, covariance 1.178 | Table 2 |

# Illustrative PK

The cendakimab population PK model is not published. For the simulations
below every treated subject receives the same illustrative PK parameters,
chosen by the maintainers so that the typical profile reproduces the median
curves of Du 2026 Figure 2 (lower panels): about 100 ug/mL at Week 4,
150 to 155 ug/mL at Week 8, a QW plateau of about 185 to 190 ug/mL, and a
QW/Q2W profile that falls to about half the QW level by Week 48, as the text
states ("concentrations declined to ~50% of QW levels by Week 48"). Because
`CL_INDIV` and the volumes are apparent values here, bioavailability is 1 and
the lag time is 0. These values carry no between-subject variability; they
exist only to exercise the exposure-response layer.

```{r illustrative-pk}
pk_typ <- tibble(
  CL_INDIV = 0.0105, # L/h
  VC_INDIV = 4.5, # L
  Q_INDIV = 0.03, # L/h
  VP_INDIV = 3.5, # L
  KA_INDIV = 0.012, # 1/h
  TLAG_INDIV = 0, # h
  FDEPOT_INDIV = 1
)
knitr::kable(pk_typ, caption = "Illustrative typical cendakimab PK (not from Du 2026).")
```

# Virtual cohort

Three arms as in the study: placebo, cendakimab 360 mg SC QW for 48 weeks, and
360 mg SC QW for 24 weeks followed by Q2W to Week 48. Each subject is
Steroid IR/I with probability 0.663 (Table 1). DD is simulated weekly from
Week 0 to Week 48 with a full 14-day diary (`NDAYS = 14`). As in the paper's
simulations, subjects whose simulated baseline DD is below 4 are replaced:
300 subjects are drawn per arm and the first 200 eligible ones are kept.

```{r cohort}
rxode2::rxSetSeed(2026)
set.seed(2026)

wk <- 168
n_draw <- 300L
n_keep <- 200L

arm_doses <- list(
  "PBO" = numeric(0),
  "CEN 360 mg QW" = seq(0, 47) * wk,
  "CEN 360 mg QW/Q2W" = c(seq(0, 23), seq(24, 46, by = 2)) * wk
)
arm_levels <- names(arm_doses)

make_arm <- function(i) {
  ids <- (i - 1L) * n_draw + seq_len(n_draw)
  obs <- tidyr::expand_grid(id = ids, time = seq(0, 48) * wk) |>
    mutate(amt = 0, evid = 0L, cmt = "latent_dysphagia_days")
  dose <- tidyr::expand_grid(id = ids, time = arm_doses[[i]]) |>
    mutate(amt = 360, evid = 1L, cmt = "depot")
  bind_rows(dose, obs) |>
    mutate(arm = arm_levels[i])
}

subjects <- tibble(
  id = seq_len(n_draw * length(arm_doses)),
  STEROID_IR = as.integer(runif(n_draw * length(arm_doses)) < 0.663)
)

events <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_along(arm_doses), make_arm)) |>
  left_join(subjects, by = "id") |>
  bind_cols(pk_typ[rep(1, 1), ]) |>
  mutate(NDAYS = 14) |>
  arrange(id, time, desc(evid))

stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(events[, c("id", "time", "evid")]))
```

# Simulation

`rxSolve()` returns the daily dysphagia probability `xi` and the CUB weight
`pinform` at every record. A DD count is drawn from the CUB distribution: with
probability `pinform` a binomial draw on `NDAYS` days, otherwise a uniform
integer on 0 to `NDAYS`. The model mean of DD given `xi` is
`pinform * NDAYS * xi + (1 - pinform) * NDAYS / 2`; it is used for the
published-mean comparisons because it removes the count-sampling noise.

```{r simulate}
mod <- readModelDb("Du_2026_cendakimab")
sim_all <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events = events, keep = c("arm", "STEROID_IR")) |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  mutate(
    week = time / wk,
    informative = runif(n()) < pinform,
    dd = ifelse(
      informative,
      rbinom(n(), NDAYS, xi),
      sample.int(15L, n(), replace = TRUE) - 1L
    ),
    dd_mean = pinform * NDAYS * xi + (1 - pinform) * NDAYS / 2
  )

eligible <- sim_all |>
  filter(week == 0, dd >= 4) |>
  group_by(arm) |>
  slice_head(n = n_keep) |>
  ungroup() |>
  select(id, dd_bl = dd)

sim <- sim_all |>
  inner_join(eligible, by = "id") |>
  mutate(arm = factor(arm, levels = arm_levels))

count(distinct(sim, id, arm), arm)
```

# Replicate published figures

## Mean DD and concentration by regimen (Figure 2)

Replicates Figure 2 of Du 2026. Lines are the mean simulated DD per week;
points are the published means at Weeks 0, 24 and 48 (Figure 2 labels).

```{r fig2-dd, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 4}
published_fig2 <- tribble(
  ~arm, ~week, ~published,
  "PBO", 0, 11.8,
  "PBO", 24, 7.26,
  "PBO", 48, 5.97,
  "CEN 360 mg QW", 0, 11.8,
  "CEN 360 mg QW", 24, 5.48,
  "CEN 360 mg QW", 48, 4.33,
  "CEN 360 mg QW/Q2W", 0, 11.8,
  "CEN 360 mg QW/Q2W", 24, 5.49,
  "CEN 360 mg QW/Q2W", 48, 4.62
) |>
  mutate(arm = factor(arm, levels = arm_levels))

mean_dd <- sim |>
  group_by(arm, week) |>
  summarise(mean_dd = mean(dd), model_mean = mean(dd_mean), .groups = "drop")

ggplot(mean_dd, aes(week, mean_dd)) +
  geom_line(aes(colour = "Simulated mean DD")) +
  geom_line(aes(y = model_mean, colour = "Mean of the model expectation")) +
  geom_point(data = published_fig2, aes(y = published, colour = "Du 2026 Figure 2")) +
  facet_wrap(~arm) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 48, 8)) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 14)) +
  labs(x = "Time after first dose (weeks)", y = "Mean dysphagia days", colour = NULL) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

```{r fig2-table}
fig2_cmp <- published_fig2 |>
  left_join(mean_dd, by = c("arm", "week")) |>
  mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (model_mean - published) / published)

# Baseline: the observed (truncated, DD >= 4) count is the comparable quantity.
fig2_cmp <- fig2_cmp |>
  mutate(simulated = ifelse(week == 0, mean_dd, model_mean)) |>
  mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (simulated - published) / published)

fig2_cmp |>
  select(arm, week, published, simulated, pct_diff) |>
  mutate(across(c(simulated, pct_diff), \(x) round(x, 2))) |>
  rename(
    "Regimen" = arm,
    "Week" = week,
    "Published mean DD" = published,
    "Simulated mean DD" = simulated,
    "Difference (%)" = pct_diff
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Mean DD: simulation vs. Du 2026 Figure 2.")

post <- fig2_cmp |> filter(week > 0)
stopifnot(
  # Structural: a wrong sign, rate or Emax moves every arm by far more.
  median(abs(post$pct_diff)) < 12,
  # Envelope across the six post-baseline arm-week means.
  max(abs(post$pct_diff)) < 30,
  abs(median(fig2_cmp$pct_diff[fig2_cmp$week == 0])) < 5
)
```

The placebo arm depends only on the published PD parameters and matches
Figure 2. The two cendakimab arms also depend on the illustrative PK, which
has no between-subject variability. With 200 subjects per arm they run a
few percent above the published means, which is within the Monte Carlo error
of a cohort this size: a 3000-subject-per-arm run of the same setup gave
4.23 (QW) against the published 4.33 at Week 48, and 6.14 against 5.97 on
placebo.

```{r fig2-pk, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 3.5}
conc <- sim |>
  filter(arm != "PBO") |>
  group_by(arm, week) |>
  summarise(Cc = median(Cc), .groups = "drop")

ggplot(conc, aes(week, Cc)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = exp(4.337), linetype = "dashed") +
  facet_wrap(~arm) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 48, 12)) +
  labs(
    x = "Time after first dose (weeks)",
    y = "Cendakimab (ug/mL)",
    caption = "Illustrative typical PK; dashed line: EC50 = 76.5 ug/mL."
  ) +
  theme_bw()
```

## Steroid IR/I vs. steroid R/N (Figure 3)

Replicates Figure 3 of Du 2026. Steroid IR/I raises Emax by a factor of
exp(0.2377) = 1.27. Du 2026 reports that at Week 48 Steroid IR/I subjects had
about 0.31 (QW) and 0.26 (QW/Q2W) fewer mean DD than Steroid R/N subjects
(Figure 3: 4.21 vs 4.53 and 4.54 vs 4.80). With 200 subjects per arm the
between-subgroup comparison is dominated by sampling noise, so the effect is
checked on the same subjects solved twice, once with every subject
`STEROID_IR = 1` and once with `STEROID_IR = 0` (same random effects).

```{r fig3, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 4}
paired_events <- events |> semi_join(eligible, by = "id")
solve_steroid <- function(value) {
  rxode2::rxSetSeed(2026)
  rxode2::rxSolve(
    mod,
    events = mutate(paired_events, STEROID_IR = value),
    keep = "arm"
  ) |>
    as.data.frame() |>
    mutate(week = time / wk, dd_mean = pinform * NDAYS * xi + (1 - pinform) * NDAYS / 2)
}
paired <- bind_rows(
  solve_steroid(1L) |> mutate(group = "Steroid IR/I"),
  solve_steroid(0L) |> mutate(group = "Steroid R/N")
) |>
  mutate(arm = factor(arm, levels = arm_levels))

# The random effects must coincide between the two solves.
eta_check <- paired |>
  filter(time == 0) |>
  select(id, group, rbase) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = group, values_from = rbase)
stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(eta_check[["Steroid IR/I"]], eta_check[["Steroid R/N"]])))

paired_mean <- paired |>
  group_by(arm, group, week) |>
  summarise(dd_mean = mean(dd_mean), .groups = "drop")

ggplot(paired_mean, aes(week, dd_mean, colour = group)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~arm) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 48, 8)) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 14)) +
  labs(x = "Time after first dose (weeks)", y = "Mean dysphagia days", colour = NULL) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")

steroid_wk48 <- paired_mean |>
  filter(week == 48) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = group, values_from = dd_mean) |>
  mutate(difference = `Steroid R/N` - `Steroid IR/I`) |>
  left_join(
    tibble(
      arm = factor(arm_levels, levels = arm_levels),
      published = c(5.94 - 5.97, 4.53 - 4.21, 4.80 - 4.54)
    ),
    by = "arm"
  )
steroid_wk48 |>
  select(arm, `Steroid IR/I`, `Steroid R/N`, difference, published) |>
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), \(x) round(x, 2))) |>
  rename(
    "Regimen" = arm,
    "R/N minus IR/I (simulated)" = difference,
    "R/N minus IR/I (Figure 3)" = published
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Week-48 mean DD by steroid status (paired solve).")

trt <- steroid_wk48 |> filter(arm != "PBO")
stopifnot(
  # The placebo arm has no drug effect, so steroid status cannot matter.
  abs(steroid_wk48$difference[steroid_wk48$arm == "PBO"]) < 1e-8,
  all(trt$difference > 0.1),
  all(trt$difference < 0.6)
)
```

## Baseline DD < 12 vs. >= 12 (Figure 4)

Replicates Figure 4 of Du 2026, stratifying subjects by their simulated
baseline DD.

```{r fig4, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 4}
strata <- sim |>
  mutate(stratum = ifelse(dd_bl >= 12, "Baseline DD >= 12", "Baseline DD < 12")) |>
  group_by(arm, stratum, week) |>
  summarise(mean_dd = mean(dd), model_mean = mean(dd_mean), n = n(), .groups = "drop")

ggplot(strata, aes(week, ifelse(week == 0, mean_dd, model_mean), colour = stratum)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~arm) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 48, 8)) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 14)) +
  labs(x = "Time after first dose (weeks)", y = "Mean dysphagia days", colour = NULL) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")

published_fig4 <- tribble(
  ~arm, ~stratum, ~week, ~published,
  "PBO", "Baseline DD < 12", 48, 3.62,
  "PBO", "Baseline DD >= 12", 48, 7.20,
  "CEN 360 mg QW", "Baseline DD < 12", 48, 1.79,
  "CEN 360 mg QW", "Baseline DD >= 12", 48, 5.62,
  "CEN 360 mg QW/Q2W", "Baseline DD < 12", 48, 2.06,
  "CEN 360 mg QW/Q2W", "Baseline DD >= 12", 48, 5.93
) |>
  mutate(arm = factor(arm, levels = arm_levels))

fig4_cmp <- published_fig4 |>
  left_join(strata, by = c("arm", "stratum", "week"))
fig4_cmp |>
  select(arm, stratum, n, published, model_mean) |>
  mutate(model_mean = round(model_mean, 2)) |>
  rename(
    "Regimen" = arm,
    "Stratum" = stratum,
    "Subjects" = n,
    "Week-48 mean DD (Figure 4)" = published,
    "Week-48 mean DD (simulated)" = model_mean
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Week-48 mean DD by baseline-DD stratum.")

gap <- fig4_cmp |>
  group_by(arm) |>
  summarise(gap = diff(model_mean), published_gap = diff(published))
stopifnot(all(gap$gap > 1.5), all(gap$gap < 7))
```

Du 2026 reports a Week-48 gap of about 3.9 days between the strata in both
cendakimab arms. The simulated gaps are of the same size; the strata are
small (a few dozen subjects below 12 days per arm), so the per-stratum means
carry more sampling noise than the arm means.

# Likelihood checks

The CUB probability mass function must sum to 1 over `k = 0..NDAYS` on a
post-baseline record, and over `k = 4..NDAYS` on a baseline record, where it
is conditioned on `DD >= 4`. It must also equal the R reference
`pi * dbinom(k, n, xi) + (1 - pi) / (n + 1)`. Each `DV` value is placed on its
own typical-value placebo subject so the solves are independent.

```{r likelihood-check}
mod_typ <- rxode2::zeroRe(rxode2::rxode(mod))
lik_events <- tidyr::expand_grid(DV = 0:14, time = c(0, 4 * wk)) |>
  mutate(
    id = row_number(),
    amt = 0,
    evid = 0L,
    cmt = "latent_dysphagia_days",
    NDAYS = 14,
    STEROID_IR = 0L
  ) |>
  bind_cols(pk_typ[rep(1, 1), ])
lik <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typ, events = lik_events, keep = "DV") |>
  as.data.frame()

lik_sum <- lik |>
  mutate(baseline = time <= 0) |>
  filter(!baseline | DV >= 4) |>
  group_by(baseline) |>
  summarise(total = sum(lik_dd))
lik_sum
stopifnot(all(abs(lik_sum$total - 1) < 1e-10))

post_lik <- lik |> filter(time > 0)
reference <- post_lik$pinform * dbinom(post_lik$DV, 14, post_lik$xi) +
  (1 - post_lik$pinform) / 15
stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(post_lik$lik_dd, reference, tolerance = 1e-10)))
```

A count outside `0..NDAYS` has zero binomial probability, and with fewer than
four diary days `P(DD <= 3) = 1`. The model clamps the count passed to
`llikBinom()` so these records evaluate instead of stopping the session.

```{r likelihood-domain-check}
edge_events <- tibble(
  id = 1:4,
  time = 4 * wk,
  DV = c(-1, 15, 2, 2),
  NDAYS = c(14, 14, 2, 0),
  amt = 0,
  evid = 0L,
  cmt = "latent_dysphagia_days",
  STEROID_IR = 0L
) |>
  bind_cols(pk_typ[rep(1, 4), ])
edge <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typ, events = edge_events, keep = "DV") |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  arrange(id) |>
  mutate(NDAYS_in = edge_events$NDAYS)
edge |> select(DV, NDAYS = NDAYS_in, pdf_binom_dd, cdf3_dd)
stopifnot(
  edge$pdf_binom_dd[1:2] == 0,
  isTRUE(all.equal(edge$pdf_binom_dd[3], dbinom(2, 2, edge$xi[3]), tolerance = 1e-12)),
  edge$pdf_binom_dd[4] == 0,
  isTRUE(all.equal(edge$cdf3_dd[3:4], c(1, 1), tolerance = 1e-12))
)
```

# Drug-effect check

On placebo the drug-effect variable stays at 1, so `drug_eff` is exactly 0.
Under QW dosing the turnover variable approaches its steady state
`1 - Cc / (EC50 + Cc)` with a half-life of 1.4 weeks; with the concentration
near its plateau late in the QW arm the two agree closely.

```{r drug-effect-check}
pbo <- sim |> filter(arm == "PBO")
stopifnot(max(abs(pbo$drug_eff)) < 1e-12)

late_qw <- sim |>
  filter(arm == "CEN 360 mg QW", week >= 40) |>
  mutate(de_ss = 1 - Cc / (exp(4.337) + Cc))
max(abs(late_qw$latent_dysphagia_days - late_qw$de_ss))
stopifnot(max(abs(late_qw$latent_dysphagia_days - late_qw$de_ss)) < 0.02)
```

# PKNCA check of the illustrative PK

Du 2026 reports no NCA results. This block confirms that the illustrative PK
gives the steady-state exposure read from Figure 2 (QW plateau about 185 to
190 ug/mL; QW/Q2W about half of QW at Week 48), over the last week (QW) and
the last two weeks (QW/Q2W) of treatment.

```{r pknca}
pk_ids <- c("CEN 360 mg QW" = 1L, "CEN 360 mg QW/Q2W" = 2L)
pk_events <- bind_rows(lapply(names(pk_ids), function(a) {
  bind_rows(
    tibble(id = pk_ids[[a]], time = arm_doses[[a]], amt = 360, evid = 1L, cmt = "depot"),
    tibble(id = pk_ids[[a]], time = seq(44 * wk, 48 * wk, by = 12), amt = 0, evid = 0L, cmt = "central")
  ) |>
    mutate(arm = a)
})) |>
  bind_cols(pk_typ[rep(1, 1), ]) |>
  mutate(NDAYS = 14, STEROID_IR = 0L) |>
  arrange(id, time, desc(evid))

pk_sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typ, events = pk_events, keep = "arm") |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  select(id, time, Cc, arm)

doses_pk <- pk_events |>
  filter(evid == 1L) |>
  select(id, time, amt, arm)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(pk_sim, Cc ~ time | arm + id)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(doses_pk, amt ~ time | arm + id)
intervals <- data.frame(
  arm = c("CEN 360 mg QW", "CEN 360 mg QW/Q2W"),
  start = c(47 * wk, 46 * wk),
  end = c(48 * wk, 48 * wk),
  cav = TRUE,
  cmax = TRUE,
  cmin = TRUE
)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))
nca_tab <- as.data.frame(nca_res) |>
  filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("cav", "cmax", "cmin")) |>
  select(arm, PPTESTCD, PPORRES) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = PPORRES)
nca_tab |>
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), \(x) round(x, 1))) |>
  rename(
    "Regimen" = arm,
    "Cav,ss (ug/mL)" = cav,
    "Cmax,ss (ug/mL)" = cmax,
    "Cmin,ss (ug/mL)" = cmin
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Steady-state NCA of the illustrative typical PK.")

cav_qw <- nca_tab$cav[nca_tab$arm == "CEN 360 mg QW"]
cav_q2w <- nca_tab$cav[nca_tab$arm == "CEN 360 mg QW/Q2W"]
stopifnot(abs(cav_qw - 190) / 190 < 0.15, abs(cav_q2w / cav_qw - 0.5) < 0.05)
```

The QW average sits a few percent above the plateau read from Figure 2,
whose curve is a weekly-sampled median that lies close to the trough; the
QW/Q2W average is half the QW average, as the paper states.

# Assumptions and deviations

- **PK layer.** The authors' population PK model is not published (Du 2026
  calls it "not shown"), and no other cendakimab population PK model has been
  published. The model keeps the authors' sequential design, with the
  per-subject PK parameters as covariate columns. The vignette's typical PK
  (CL 0.0105 L/h, Vc 4.5 L, Q 0.03 L/h, Vp 3.5 L, ka 0.012 1/h, no lag,
  F = 1) was chosen by the maintainers to reproduce the median concentration
  curves of Du 2026 Figure 2. It is illustrative only, with no between-subject
  variability, so the simulated cendakimab arms cannot reproduce the PK-driven
  spread of the published simulations.
- **Placebo onset in closed form.** `PBO(t) = exp(-kPBOKON * t)` replaces the
  ODE `DADT(4) = -PBOKON*A(4)` with `A_0(4) = 1`; the two are identical when
  the solve starts at the first dose (`t = 0`). A record before the first
  dose would give `PBO > 1` in the closed form, while NONMEM starts the ODE at
  the first record.
- **Half-lives as rate constants.** Table 2 reports the placebo-onset and
  drug-onset half-lives in weeks. The model stores
  `log(log(2) / (168 * t_half))` per hour, the conversion in the NONMEM code;
  the IIV is on the placebo rate constant, as in `PBOKON = POPPBOKON*EXP(ETA(2))`.
- **Count domain.** The NONMEM code evaluates `BINOMIALCDF` and the binomial
  density only on observed counts in `0..NDAYS`. In rxode2 an out-of-range
  count in `llikBinom()` stops the R session, so the model clamps the count
  and multiplies by an indicator. The likelihood is unchanged for every
  in-range record, and a count outside the range gets zero binomial mass.
  Baseline records still need `NDAYS >= 4`, the enrolment criterion.
- **Placebo subjects' PK columns.** The NONMEM code sets every PK parameter to
  1 for placebo subjects. Placebo subjects receive no doses, so the values
  are irrelevant as long as they are positive.
- **Simulated cohort.** Only steroid status enters the final model. Each
  subject is Steroid IR/I with probability 0.663 (Table 1), the diary is
  complete (`NDAYS = 14`), and there is no dropout, as in the paper's
  simulations. Du 2026 drew 1000 subjects per replicate over 500 replicates
  with parameter uncertainty; the vignette uses 200 subjects per arm and the
  point estimates.
- **Endpoint names.** The count output is `dysphagia_days` and the
  drug-effect latent state is `latent_dysphagia_days`; `xi` is the daily
  dysphagia probability and `dd_binom_mean = NDAYS * xi` is the NONMEM `IPRE`.

# Errata

- **Equation 10 width factor.** Equation 10 prints the width factor of the
  logit-transformed IIV as `e^thetaLGT2`. The Supporting Information NONMEM
  code multiplies by `LGT2 = THETA(8)` directly
  (`ETABASET = (EXP(LGT1+ETABASE)/(1+EXP(LGT1+ETABASE))-LGT1T)*LGT2`) with a
  lower bound of 0 on THETA(8), and the Table 2 estimate of 61.24 is only
  plausible on the linear scale (`e^61.24` would be about 4e26). The model
  follows the code. Equation 10 also writes `LGT1` for the term subtracted
  inside the brackets; the code subtracts `LGT1T = expit(LGT1)`, which is the
  definition in Equation 9.
- **IIV structure.** The Abstract states that IIV was estimated for baseline
  DD, maximum placebo effect and maximum drug effect. The final model in
  Table 2 and the NONMEM code has IIV on BASE and on the placebo-onset rate
  constant only (with their covariance); IIV on Pmax and Emax was explored
  (Table S3) and is not in the final model. The model follows Table 2.
- **Covariance label.** The Table 2 footnote calls the `BASE-kPBOKON` entry a
  correlation. The value 1.178 is the off-diagonal element of the NONMEM
  `$OMEGA BLOCK(2)`, a covariance; the implied correlation is
  1.178 / sqrt(4.309 * 4.041) = 0.28.
- **Effect signs.** Equation 2 subtracts the placebo and drug effects; the
  NONMEM code adds `PBOEFF = -1*PMAX*(1-A(4))` and `DEEFF = -1*EMAX*(1-A(5))`.
  The two are the same.
- No correction notice for Du 2026 was found on Europe PMC (checked
  2026-11-11).
